question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $23,$ the additive inverse of $-49$ modulo $23$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-49$ modulo $23$ is the integer $0\le x<23$ such that

$$
x+(-49)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,23).
$$

First, we note that $-49≡20\,(\text{mod}\,23):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-49 & ≡(-3)\cdot 23+20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23) \\  & ≡(-3)\cdot 0+20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23) \\  & ≡20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-20+20≡0,$ so $x≡-20\,(\text{mod}\,23).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23) \\  & ≡0-20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23) \\  & ≡23-20 & \,(\text{mod}\,23) \\  & ≡3 & \,(\text{mod}\,23)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-49$ modulo $23$ is $3.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-49+3≡-46≡(-2)\cdot 23≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,23)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
